name: Implantable brain-computer interfaces
title: Implantable brain-computer interfaces: is a pivotal trial next?
question: Are implantable brain-computer interfaces close to approval for patients?
answer: Cyberkinetics took the BrainGate implant into its first human trial and sold off its BrainGate business and assets in 2008-2009 without a path to market. Synchron, Neuralink, Paradromics and Precision Neuroscience now have implants in human studies. The dated trigger is a pivotal trial, the last step before FDA approval; the board watches ClinicalTrials.gov for one.
verdict_reason: Early feasibility studies are running; no pivotal trial is registered yet.

constraint.name: A regulatory path for permanent implants
constraint.detail: A BCI needs proof of long-term safety and benefit in a pivotal trial before premarket approval; feasibility studies are not enough.

crossing.text: First pivotal trial of a permanent BCI implant registered.

graveyard.name: Cyberkinetics Neurotechnology Systems
graveyard.how: Sold its BrainGate business and other assets in 2008-2009

winners.note: endovascular implant; completed the COMMAND early feasibility study
